question: In an attempt to create other selective dopamine 1 (D1) agonists, a small pharmaceutical company created a cell-based chemical screen that involved three modified receptors - alpha 1 (A1), beta 1 (B1), and D1. In the presence of D1 stimulation, the cell would produce an mRNA that codes for a fluorescent protein; however, if the A1 or B1 receptors are also stimulated at the same time, the cells would degrade the mRNA of the fluorescent protein thereby preventing it from being produced. Which of the following would best serve as a positive control for this experiment?
analysis: In this experiment, a positive control should be a compound that selectively activates the D1 receptor without affecting the A1 or B1 receptors. Bromocriptine (opa) is a D2 receptor agonist and does not serve as a positive control for D1. Dobutamine (opb) primarily stimulates B1 receptors and would not be appropriate. Dopamine (opc) can activate D1 receptors but also affects A1 and B1 receptors, making it unsuitable. Epinephrine (opd) activates both A1 and B1 receptors, which would interfere with the experiment. Fenoldopam (ope) is a selective D1 agonist and would serve as the best positive control as it specifically activates D1 receptors without affecting A1 or B1 receptors.
